title: A 60 per cent CGT discount, death taxes and a land tax could deliver real reform (page title: A 60pc CGT discount and taxing gains at death make a better tax bargain) - Cathal Leslie, AFR, 9/10 Nov 2026
what_was_fetched: One ordinary GET of the AFR URL (HTTP 200): headline, standfirst, byline, date, tags, JSON-LD NewsArticle and the first two body paragraphs only; rest paywalled and not pursued (saved: item1-afr-article-page.html, item1-afr-headers.txt, item1-afr-openly-visible-text.txt). Open-copy search on prosper.org.au (home, /news/, /media/, /blog/, site search for 'Leslie' and 'capital gains', team page) found NO republication of the op-ed and no link to it; no personal site for Leslie located; no social accounts checked (none surfaced as serving text). Also read, as context only, Prosper's 10 Sep 2026 Leslie submission on the CGT/negative gearing Tranche 2 bill (item1-prosper-cgt-negative-gearing-submission.txt) and the Creighton Henry George address (item1-prosper-land-tax-past-present-prospects.txt); neither is the op-ed.
verdict: REJECT - no open copy; the openly readable portion contains no concrete proposal, figure or land-tax element that could carry an attributed sentence; revisit only if Prosper republishes the text.
claim_grade: D for any content beyond the headline (unreadable); what is readable is a headline/standfirst assertion of an opinion. Source tier: Cathal Leslie is Senior Economist, Prosper Australia (per prosper.org.au team page and his Prosper submissions) = Tier 2 advocacy-body author, origin/proponent only, never support (EDITORIAL 4c). AFR is a Tier 1 outlet as publisher but the piece is opinion by an advocate.
content_summary: Readable: headline asserts 'a 60 per cent CGT discount, death taxes and a land tax could deliver real reform' (JSON-LD headline; the page headline omits land tax). Standfirst: Labor should revive Keating's 1980s proposal to stop people sitting on assets until bequeathed to children tax-free. Body para 1: he argued six months ago (AFR, 28 May 2026) that the budget was a poorly crafted tax increase dressed up as intergenerational reform. Para 2: with polls dipping and the cash rate at an 18-year high, government can change course with limited damage because most CGT measures take effect only next financial year. NO figures, no revenue estimates, no sources, no land-tax design (state vs federal, rates, stamp-duty replacement), nothing on incidence is visible. The 60 per cent discount, tax on gains at death and land tax are only named in the headline. Context from Prosper's own 10 Sep 2026 submission: the Government's 2026 budget CGT reform (changes taking effect 1 July 2027, with a 30 June 2027 apportionment/valuation date, loss quarantining on residential investment property, and a 'new residential dwelling' concession which Prosper wants scrapped) - the submission contains no mention of 60 per cent, death/bequest taxation, Keating or land tax; so the op-ed's proposal is not corroborated by any open text.
